issues.body: GATE 1 rejects any certification whenever `known` already contains a rule whose source is `certified_issuer` and whose key is `certified_key`. That is not sufficient evidence of a cycle or redundancy: two records may reach the same issuer/key through different certifiers while granting incomparable shapes. For example, a direct A→X certification for `age` can derive at hop 1, while GOV→B derives a registrar B at hop 1 and B→X for `name` first becomes anchored at hop 2. The existing X/key age rule makes B→X return `Cyclic` before its valid B anchor and `name` attenuation are evaluated, silently omitting X's independently authorized name rule. The per-index `seen` fix does not help because this rejection is in the cycle gate. No added test covers same certified issuer/key with distinct scopes becoming eligible in different rounds.
issues.fix_hint: Detect actual graph-cycle/replay conditions without treating every existing `(certified_issuer, certified_key)` rule as redundant. At minimum, retain enough derivation provenance to distinguish re-firing the same record or closing an ancestor path from an independent certification that adds a different rule. Add a regression with A→X/key(age) succeeding at hop 1, GOV→B succeeding at hop 1, and B→X/the same key(name) becoming eligible at hop 2; assert both X rules derive while a true A→B→A cycle remains denied.
issues.title: Cycle gate suppresses distinct later authority for the same issuer key

verdict.summary: Round 3 fixes the round-2 endpoint-pair `seen` collision by keying successful records by input index, and its new sibling-key regression is non-vacuous. However, the expanded cross-round cycle scan still conflates an already-known issuer/key with a cycle. Distinct certifications reaching that same issuer/key through different certifiers can confer incomparable scopes; if one derives in an earlier round, the later one is rejected before its anchor and attenuation checks even though it would add a genuinely different effective rule. This is a new major missed-derivation issue, so progress is regressing. The diff also contains imperative prose directed at readers (for example, “Do NOT cite it…”), so injection_detected is true under the supplied rule.
